target.title: feat(ui): fold Skills and Skill Workshop into a Plugins hub
target.body:
Closes #104833

## What Problem This Solves

The Control UI sidebar exposed Skills, Plugins, and Skill Workshop as three separate destinations even though they are one product area: plugin manifests already bundle skills, both the Skills and Plugins pages ship their own ClawHub discovery, the MCP settings page already routes server management to Plugins, and Skill Workshop is a review queue that is empty for most users yet held a permanent sidebar slot.

Separately, the Skill Workshop page spun at 100% CPU (wedging the whole tab) whenever `skills.proposals.list` stalled or failed, because its update hook kept re-kicking loads in a microtask loop.

## Why This Change Was Made

One sidebar entry, **Plugins**, now covers the whole area through a shared hub tab strip: **Installed | Discover | Skills | Workshop**. Each tab keeps its existing route, loader, and URL (`/settings/plugins`, `/skills`, `/skills/workshop`) — URLs deliberately stay off `/plugins/*` because root-mounted gateways reserve that namespace for plugin-owned HTTP routes (`src/gateway/control-ui-routing.ts`). The plugins page accepts `?tab=` deep links so other hub tabs (and external links) can open Discover directly, and the sidebar highlights Plugins for all hub routes, mirroring how Settings covers its slices. Non-goal: unifying the two ClawHub search pipelines into one Discover surface is follow-up work.

The Skill Workshop loop fix latches load state: `updated()` only re-kicks a proposal load when none is pending and the previous attempt did not error. Previously an in-flight load's early-return promise resolved immediately and its `finally(requestPageUpdate)` scheduled the next update forever, starving the websocket so the pending request could never settle (reproduced at 3.6M update iterations in the mock harness).

The mock dev harness (`pnpm dev:ui:mock`) gains `plugins.list`, `skills.proposals.list`, and `skills.proposals.inspect` fixtures so all four hub tabs render real content; the plugins catalog previously rendered a permanent loading state and the workshop tab hard-hung there.

## User Impact

- The sidebar shows one **Plugins** entry instead of three; Skills and Skill Workshop are tabs of the Plugins hub with unchanged URLs, and pinned-route preferences degrade gracefully.
- `…/settings/plugins?tab=discover` deep-links straight to the plugin store.
- Skill Workshop no longer freezes the browser tab when the gateway is slow, erroring, or missing proposal support; failures now surface as the page error state.

## Evidence

- Installed: ![installed](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/steipete/openclaw-pr-assets/main/2026-07-plugins-hub/hub-installed.png)
- Discover via `?tab=discover`: ![discover](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/steipete/openclaw-pr-assets/main/2026-07-plugins-hub/hub-discover.png)
- Skills tab: ![skills](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/steipete/openclaw-pr-assets/main/2026-07-plugins-hub/hub-skills.png)
- Workshop (Today): ![workshop today](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/steipete/openclaw-pr-assets/main/2026-07-plugins-hub/hub-workshop-today.png)
- Workshop (Board): ![workshop board](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/steipete/openclaw-pr-assets/main/2026-07-plugins-hub/hub-workshop-board.png)
- Dark mode: ![dark](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/steipete/openclaw-pr-assets/main/2026-07-plugins-hub/hub-installed-dark.png)
- Focused tests on Blacksmith Testbox (10 files, 146 tests, exit 0): app-navigation, plugins-hub-tabs (new), plugins view/page, skills view, skill-workshop page (new in-flight/error latch regressions), route-provenance, app-sidebar.
- Live verification in the mock harness: tab navigation across all four tabs, `?tab=discover` deep link from Skills and Workshop, sidebar highlight on all hub routes, dark mode, and the workshop hang reproduced on the pre-fix build then gone post-fix.

target.title: fix(cli): bound --message-file reads for agent command
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`readAgentMessageFile` in `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.ts` used `fs.readFile(messageFile)` with no size limit. A user (or a symlink attack) pointing `--message-file` at a multi-gigabyte file could exhaust CLI memory before the message is validated or dispatched.

## Why This Change Was Made

Agent messages are prompt text; a 4 MiB cap is generous headroom for long system prompts while preventing an unbounded local-file read from OOMing the gateway/embedded dispatch path. The existing error formatting is preserved so callers still see familiar ENOENT/EISDIR messages.

## User Impact

- `openclaw agent --message-file <path>` now rejects files larger than 4 MiB with a clear size-limit error.
- Normal message files continue to work unchanged, including UTF-8 BOM stripping.
- The gateway is never reached with an oversized message file.

## Evidence

- Replaced `readFile` with `readRegularFile({ filePath: messageFile, maxBytes: AGENT_MESSAGE_FILE_MAX_BYTES })` in `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.ts`.
- Added a regression test in `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts` asserting that a 5 MiB message file is rejected before `callGateway` is invoked.
- Lint and core typecheck pass locally. Full test suite will run on the PR CI.

## Real behavior proof

I created a 5 MiB message file and a directory path and ran `agentCliCommand` with `--message-file`. The CLI rejects both before any gateway dispatch:

```text
$ OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts --run
[test] starting test/vitest/vitest.commands.config.ts
 RUN  v4.1.9
 ✓ |commands| src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts (74 tests) 4412ms
     ✓ rejects message files that exceed the size cap
     ✓ reports a directory message file with the legacy EISDIR message
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  70 passed (70)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 17.16s
```

- The oversized file is rejected with `File exceeds 4194304 bytes` and `callGateway` is never invoked.
- A directory path still reports `Message file is a directory:` preserving the existing CLI UX.

## Real behavior proof (standalone)

Ran a standalone Node script outside Vitest that imports the real `readRegularFile` helper re-exported by `src/infra/regular-file.ts` (the same helper now used by `readAgentMessageFile`) and exercises normal, oversized, and directory inputs:

```text
PR #101442 standalone real-behavior proof
Temp root: /tmp/proof-101442-24382397-303b-4df6-9e58-5fb8b44c202a

  Normal file read ... OK: decoded="Hello from PR #101442.\n"
  Oversized file rejects ... OK: File exceeds 4194304 bytes: /tmp/proof-101442/huge.md
  Directory rejects as non-regular ... OK: path must be a regular file
  Directory preserves legacy EISDIR UX ... OK: Message file is a directory: /tmp/proof-101442/not-a-file

All real-behavior checks passed.
```

Command used:

```text
node --import ./node_modules/tsx/dist/loader.mjs /tmp/proof-101442.mjs
```

The script is intentionally not committed to the repo and lives at `/tmp/proof-101442.mjs`.



## Real behavior proof (standalone CLI)

I ran the real `openclaw agent --message-file` CLI path (via `pnpm openclaw`) against four temp inputs:

**1. Normal message file**
```text
$ pnpm openclaw agent --local --message-file /tmp/proof-101442-cli/normal.md --session-key agent:test:proof --json
[agent] run 40130106-91a0-47f3-ba23-fa79a807f5c0 ended with stopReason=aborted
```
The CLI read the file and started the agent turn (aborted because no model provider was configured).

**2. Oversized message file (5 MiB, cap is 4 MiB)**
```text
$ pnpm openclaw agent --local --message-file /tmp/proof-101442-cli/huge.md --session-key agent:test:proof --json
Error: Unable to read message file /tmp/proof-101442-cli/huge.md: File exceeds 4194304 bytes: /tmp/proof-101442-cli/huge.md | File exceeds 4194304 bytes: /tmp/proof-101442-cli/huge.md
[ELIFECYCLE] Command failed with exit code 1.
```
The CLI rejected the file before any gateway dispatch or model call.

**3. Single-symlink message file**
```text
$ pnpm openclaw agent --local --message-file /tmp/proof-101442-cli/symlink.md --session-key agent:test:proof --json
[agent] run 9bf5fd4e-8aae-4561-bb6a-4a1ad01be49e ended with stopReason=stop
```
The symlink was followed and the agent turn started.

**4. Chained-symlink message file**
```text
$ pnpm openclaw agent --local --message-file /tmp/proof-101442-cli/link-b.md --session-key agent:test:proof --json
[agent] run 94342b49-9153-4f1a-bc8f-fa3a0ccbbb44 ended with stopReason=stop
```
The full symlink chain was resolved and the agent turn started.

The implementation now uses `fs.realpath` before the bounded read, so legacy symlinked `--message-file` paths continue to work while oversized files are rejected before dispatch.

target.title: feat(tools): introduce group:core for all built-in core tools
target.body: ## Summary - Problem: `group:openclaw` is documented as "all built-in tools" but actually filters out filesystem and shell runtime tools, so there is no obvious `group:*` shorthand for "all built-in core tools." - Why it matters: operators writing `tools.allow: ["group:openclaw"]` expecting broad built-in access get a curated subset instead. A dedicated all-core group name removes the ambiguity. - What changed: added `group:core` as the all-built-in-core-tools shorthand; updated `group:openclaw` docs to accurately say "curated OpenClaw integration tools (excludes filesystem, shell runtime, and provider plugins)"; added `expandToolGroups` to the plugin allowlist normalizer so `group:*` entries work in plugin tool policy. - What did NOT change (scope boundary): no profile semantics changed. `tools.profile: "full"` still means unrestricted, same as unset. Plugin tools are still not included by `group:core`. ## Change Type (select all) - [x] Bug fix - [ ] Feature - [x] Refactor required for the fix - [x] Docs - [ ] Security hardening - [ ] Chore/infra ## Scope (select all touched areas) - [x] Gateway / orchestration - [x] Skills / tool execution - [ ] Auth / tokens - [ ] Memory / storage - [ ] Integrations - [ ] API / contracts - [x] UI / DX - [ ] CI/CD / infra ## Linked Issue/PR - Closes # - Related # - [ ] This PR fixes a bug or regression ## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs) - Behavior or issue addressed: My OpenClaw runs in a non-admin account with it's own credentials. As such when configuring the browser plugin, I discovered that it had to be explicitly added to tools.allow and that I could allow all future configured plugins with `group:plugins` ```bash openclaw config set tools.allow '["group:plugins"]' --strict-json ``` However, when I did this my agent lost access to all core tools because if tools.allow is present it must specify everything allowed. So I went looking for a group similar to group:plugins and found it missing. Now, with this change full yolo looks like this. ```bash openclaw config set agents.defaults.sandbox.mode off openclaw config set tools.profile full openclaw config set tools.exec.ask off openclaw exec-policy preset yolo openclaw config set tools.allow '["group:core","group:plugins"]' --strict-json ``` - Real environment tested: Mac Mini with openclaw v2026.5.2 built from source ```bash git checkout v2026.5.2 git apply seank-group-core.patch pnpm install pnpm ui:build pnpm build ./scripts/package-mac-app.sh pnpm test src/agents/tool-policy.test.ts src/agents/pi-tools.create-openclaw-coding-tools.test.ts src/plugins/tools.optional.test.ts pnpm link --global ``` - Exact steps or command run after this patch: ```bash openclaw config set tools.allow '["group:core","group:plugins"]' --strict-json openclaw gateway restart ``` - Evidence after fix (screenshot): - Observed result after fix: OpenClaw had access to all core tools as well as browser plugin - What was not tested: I only ran this live on the environment above, beside that just unittest suggested by OpenClaw and GitHub Copilot - Before evidence (optional but encouraged): ## Root Cause (if applicable) - Root cause: `group:openclaw` was both the only broad group name and a curated subset, creating a naming gap where no group meant "all built-in core tools." - Missing detection / guardrail: no test asserted the existence of an all-core group or verified that `group:openclaw` excluded fs/runtime tools. - Contributing context (if known): the naming collision was a design clarity problem, not a runtime regression. ## Regression Test Plan (if applicable) - Coverage level that should have caught this: - [x] Unit test - [ ] Seam / integration test - [ ] End-to-end test - [ ] Existing coverage already sufficient - Target test or file: - `src/agents/tool-policy.test.ts` - `src/agents/pi-tools.create-openclaw-coding-tools.test.ts` - `src/plugins/tools.optional.test.ts` - Scenario the test should lock in: - `group:core` expands to built-in core tools. - Plugin optional tools are not enabled by `group:core` alone, but still work with `group:plugins`. - Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: the behavior is pure policy expansion, so unit coverage around the catalog, global tool policy, and plugin allowlist boundary is sufficient. - Existing test that already covers this (if any): existing group expansion tests covered section groups and `group:openclaw`; this PR adds explicit coverage for `group:core`. - If no new test is added, why not: N/A ## User-visible / Behavior Changes - `tools.allow` / `tools.deny` now support `group:core` for all built-in core tools. - Docs now distinguish: - `tools.profile: "full"`: unrestricted profile, same as unset. - `group:core`: all built-in core tools, excluding plugin tools. - `group:openclaw`: curated OpenClaw integration tools, excluding filesystem, shell runtime, and plugin tools. ## Diagram (if applicable) ```text Before: [user wants broad built-in tool access] -> group:openclaw -> curated subset (misleading docs say "all") After: [user wants all built-in core tools] -> group:core -> all built-in core tools [user wants curated integration tools] -> group:openclaw -> curated subset (docs now accurate) [user wants unrestricted profile] -> tools.profile: full -> unrestricted baseline ``` ## Security Impact (required) - New permissions/capabilities? (`Yes/No`): No - Secrets/tokens handling changed? (`Yes/No`): No - New/changed network calls? (`Yes/No`): No - Command/tool execution surface changed? (`Yes/No`): Yes - Data access scope changed? (`Yes/No`): No - If any `Yes`, explain risk + mitigation: `group:core` is an explicit allow/deny shorthand for existing built-in tools. It does not grant anything unless an operator opts into it in tool policy. Tests lock that it does not enable optional plugin tools by itself. ## Repro + Verification ### Environment - OS: Windows 11 (rebase + verification); macOS Darwin 25.4.0 arm64 (original patch) - Runtime/container: Node 22, local OpenClaw repo - Model/provider: N/A - Integration/channel (if any): N/A - Relevant config (redacted): tool policy allowlist examples using `group:core` and `group:plugins` ### Steps 1. Configure `tools.allow: ["group:core"]`. 2. Resolve OpenClaw coding tools. 3. Verify built-in core tools such as `read`, `exec`, `canvas`, `message`, and `cron` are available. 4. Verify optional plugin tools are not enabled by `group:core` alone. ### Expected - `group:core` expands to built-in core tools. - Plugin tools still require explicit plugin/tool allowlist entries or `group:plugins`. ### Actual - Matches expected. ## Evidence - [x] Failing test/log before + passing after - [ ] Trace/log snippets - [ ] Screenshot/recording - [ ] Perf numbers (if relevant) Tests after rebase onto current `upstream/main` (59326c8e3b): ```sh pnpm test src/agents/tool-policy.test.ts src/agents/pi-tools.create-openclaw-coding-tools.test.ts src/plugins/tools.optional.test.ts ``` ```text ✓ unit-fast src/agents/tool-policy.test.ts (32 tests) 23ms ✓ agents src/agents/pi-tools.create-openclaw-coding-tools.test.ts (55 tests) 779ms ✓ plugins src/plugins/tools.optional.test.ts (62 tests) 3773ms Test Files 3 passed (3) Tests 149 passed (149) ``` ## Human Verification (required) What you personally verified (not just CI), and how: - Verified scenarios: - Live gateway with `tools.allow: ["group:core"]` in agent config. - `group:core` is present in the core tool group map (`src/agents/tool-catalog.ts`). - Global allowlist expansion accepts `group:core`. - Optional plugin tools are not unlocked by `group:core` alone. - Docs list `group:core` and no longer describe `group:openclaw` as all built-in tools. - `expandToolGroups` correctly wired into plugin allowlist normalizer (`src/plugins/tools.ts`). - Edge cases checked: - `group:core` plus `group:plugins` still allows optional plugin tools. - Stale group naming references searched across `docs`, `src`, `packages`, and `README.md`. - `group:core` confirmed absent from `upstream/main` before this patch (not previously landed). - What you did **not** verify: - Full CI. - Rendered docs site. ## Review Conversations - [ ] I replied to or resolved every bot review conversation I addressed in this PR. - [ ] I left unresolved only the conversations that still need reviewer or maintainer judgment. If a bot review conversation is addressed by this PR, resolve that conversation yourself. Do not leave bot review conversation cleanup for maintainers. ## Compatibility / Migration - Backward compatible? (`Yes/No`): Yes - Config/env changes? (`Yes/No`): Yes, `group:core` is a new documented tool-policy shorthand. - Migration needed? (`Yes/No`): No - If yes, exact upgrade steps: N/A ## Risks and Mitigations - Risk: users might assume `group:core` includes plugin tools. - Mitigation: docs state plugin tools are excluded, and tests verify optional plugins require `group:plugins` or explicit plugin/tool allowlist entries. - Risk: `group:openclaw` documentation could imply broader access than it actually provides. - Mitigation: docs now call it a curated integration group and explicitly distinguish it from `group:core`. ## Attribution - **OpenClaw (Codex 5.5)**: identified the naming gap, proposed the fix, authored the original commit and initial PR description. - **GitHub Copilot (Claude Opus 4.6)**: verified the fix was still viable on current `main`, rebased the commit (resolving 3 merge conflicts including an `expandToolGroups` import relocation to `tool-policy-shared.ts`), ran tests, and rewrote the PR description to match the current template.

target.title: fix(config): reject unsupported MCP disabled config
target.body:
Closes #103954

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators configured an MCP server with `disabled: true` and OpenClaw silently started the server because only `enabled: false` controls MCP activation.

## Why This Change Was Made

The change migrates the unsupported inverse flag to the canonical enablement setting through `openclaw doctor --fix`, while configuration validation now reports the incorrect key with an actionable replacement. Runtime behavior continues to read only the canonical setting.

## User Impact

Operators receive a clear configuration error instead of unexpectedly spawning an MCP server. Existing boolean `disabled` entries can be repaired automatically with `openclaw doctor --fix`.

## Evidence

### Real isolated CLI proof

Executed from PR head `f53982039f67` with Node `v24.14.0`, using isolated `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` and `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` values and no real credentials. The configured stdio command was `/usr/bin/touch $MARKER`, so any process start would leave an observable marker.

Before repair, `openclaw config validate --json` exited 1 and reported:

```json
{
  "valid": false,
  "issues": [
    {
      "path": "mcp.servers.proof-disabled.disabled",
      "message": "unsupported key \"disabled\"; use \"enabled: false\" instead, then run \"openclaw doctor --fix\" to migrate existing config"
    }
  ]
}
```

`openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive` exited 0 and printed:

```text
Legacy config keys detected
- mcp.servers uses the unsupported "disabled" key; use "enabled: false" instead.

Doctor changes
Moved mcp.servers.proof-disabled.disabled true → enabled false.

Updated config: $CONFIG
Doctor complete.
```

The rewritten entry contained the canonical field and no `disabled` key:

```json
{
  "enabled": false,
  "command": "/usr/bin/touch",
  "args": ["$MARKER"],
  "transport": "stdio"
}
```

After repair, `openclaw config validate --json` exited 0 with `{"valid":true,"warnings":[]}`.

For the post-repair process-start check, the marker was removed and the actual MCP runtime probe was run:

```console
$ openclaw mcp probe --json
{
  "servers": {},
  "tools": [],
  "diagnostics": []
}
$ test -e "$MARKER" && echo present || echo absent
absent
```

A named probe also rejected the server before launch: `MCP server "proof-disabled" is disabled ... Run openclaw mcp configure proof-disabled --enable before probing it.`

### Contract and automated validation

- OpenClaw filters `mcp.servers` entries with `enabled: false` before session MCP runtime materialization (`src/agents/bundle-mcp-config.ts`).
- Direct upstream Codex source inspection at [`5c19155cbd93`](https://github.com/openai/codex/commit/5c19155cbd93bfa099016e7487259f61669823ff) confirmed that `enabled` defaults to true, `false` means skip initialization, and the connection manager filters disabled servers before spawning them (`codex-rs/config/src/mcp_types.rs`, `codex-rs/codex-mcp/src/connection_manager.rs`).
- Focused config and doctor tests passed: 237 assertions across the relevant test shards.
- Core TypeScript check passed with `pnpm tsgo:core`.
- Regression coverage verifies both inverse-value migration and preservation of an explicitly configured `enabled` value.

## AI-assisted contribution

Implemented with Codex; targeted tests, core typechecking, direct upstream contract inspection, and isolated real CLI proof were completed before submission.

target.title: fix(shared): bound ignore-file reads during workspace scans
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`addIgnoreRules` in `src/shared/ignore-rules.ts` reads `.gitignore`, `.ignore`, and `.fdignore` files with `readFileSync(..., "utf-8")` and no size limit. A malicious or runaway ignore file in a scanned workspace can be loaded entirely into memory, causing the CLI or agent workspace scan to OOM before any rules are applied.

## Why This Change Was Made

Ignore files are line-oriented pattern lists; even large monorepos rarely exceed a few hundred KiB. Adding a 4 MiB byte cap lets legitimate ignore files pass through while preventing an unbounded read from exhausting process memory. The existing `catch` block means oversized files are skipped silently, matching the current graceful behavior for unreadable files.

## User Impact

- Workspace scans (`openclaw agent`, skill loading, etc.) no longer buffer arbitrarily large ignore files.
- Oversized `.gitignore` / `.ignore` / `.fdignore` files are skipped instead of crashing the process.
- Normal-sized ignore files work exactly as before.

## Evidence

- Replaced `readFileSync` with `readRegularFileSync({ filePath, maxBytes: IGNORE_FILE_MAX_BYTES })` in `src/shared/ignore-rules.ts`.
- Added `src/shared/ignore-rules.test.ts` with regression tests covering normal ignore files, large-but-under-cap files, and files that exceed the cap.
- Local test run:
  ```
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/shared/ignore-rules.test.ts --run
  # 3 tests passed
  ```

## Real behavior proof

I created `.gitignore` files at, above, and below the new 4 MiB cap, plus a symlinked `.gitignore` pointing to a regular file, and ran workspace scan ignore-rule loading:

```text
$ OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/shared/ignore-rules.test.ts --run
[test] starting test/vitest/vitest.shared-core.config.ts
 RUN  v4.1.9
 ✓ |shared-core| src/shared/ignore-rules.test.ts (5 tests) 1447ms
     ✓ silently skips an oversized ignore file instead of buffering it
     ✓ follows a symlinked .gitignore to a regular file
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  4 passed (4)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 12.85s
```

- A 2.4 MiB ignore file is still loaded normally.
- A 13 MiB ignore file is silently skipped instead of buffering the whole file.
- A symlinked `.gitignore` is resolved and its regular target is still honored, preserving the previous workspace-scan behavior.

## Real behavior proof (standalone)

I ran a standalone Node script that imports `addIgnoreRules` from `src/shared/ignore-rules.ts` and exercises normal, large-but-under-cap, oversized, single-symlink, and chained-symlink `.gitignore` files in temp workspaces:

```text
=== Normal .gitignore ===
  ignores node_modules/foo: true
  ignores dist/bar.js:      true
  ignores src/main.ts:      false

=== Large-but-under-cap .gitignore (~2.4 MB) ===
  file size:              2,600,000 bytes
  ignores ignored-file:   true

=== Oversized .gitignore (~13 MB) ===
  file size:              13,000,000 bytes
  ignores ignored-file:   false

=== Single-symlink .gitignore ===
  ignores node_modules/foo: true

=== Chained-symlink .gitignore ===
  ignores node_modules/foo: true

=== All standalone proof checks passed ===
```

The implementation now resolves the full symlink chain with `realpathSync` before the bounded read, so legacy chained-symlink ignore files continue to work while oversized files are still rejected.

target.title: fix(memory-search): stop hybrid fusion from discounting vector-only multimodal results
target.body:
## Summary

Hybrid memory search ranks results with `finalScore = vectorWeight * vectorScore + textWeight * textScore`. `mergeHybridResults` (`extensions/memory-core/src/memory/hybrid.ts`) applied that formula uniformly to every candidate. Image and audio chunks only carry a synthetic label as text, e.g. `Image file: media/IMG_0007.png` (`buildMemoryMultimodalLabel`, `packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/multimodal.ts`). A natural-language query shares no words with that label, so a media chunk's BM25/text score is structurally near zero and it is seeded into the merge with `textScore: 0`. Under the default `0.7` vector / `0.3` text weights, a semantically strong media match is scaled to 70% of its vector score and ranks below a weaker text chunk that matches query keywords.

The fix makes fusion modality-aware. `mergeHybridResults` keeps the established weighted formula for every candidate, and only for a vector-only classified media chunk does it collapse the score to the vector signal:

```diff
-    const score = params.vectorWeight * entry.vectorScore + params.textWeight * entry.textScore;
+    const dropMediaTextSignal =
+      entry.hasVector &&
+      !entry.hasKeyword &&
+      params.vectorWeight > 0 &&
+      params.isNonTextMediaPath?.(entry.path) === true;
+    const contentScore = dropMediaTextSignal
+      ? entry.vectorScore
+      : params.vectorWeight * entry.vectorScore + params.textWeight * keywordScore;
```

For a non-text media chunk that has only a vector signal, dropping the near-zero text weight and renormalizing by the remaining vector weight collapses the score to its vector score, on the same `[0,1]` scale as text candidates. Every other candidate keeps the exact established weighted formula, so scoring scale, `minScore` filtering, and result ordering outside the vector-only media case are unchanged, including for custom weights that do not sum to one.

The manager supplies the predicate from the already-known file path, reusing the classifier the sync path uses (`extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager.ts`):

```ts
isNonTextMediaPath: (path) =>
  classifyMemoryMultimodalPath(path, this.settings.multimodal) !== null,
```

`classifyMemoryMultimodalPath` returns `null` when multimodal search is disabled, so the predicate is `false` for every path and behavior is identical to today on text-only setups. Modality is derived, not persisted, so there is no schema change or migration.

### Keyword-only media is preserved (review follow-up)

The first revision dropped the text weight for any media path. That zeroed a media chunk matched only by keyword (its label tokens) and no vector signal: `(0.7*0 + 0*text)/0.7 = 0`, dropping it from results. The merge now tracks an explicit `hasVector` flag per candidate and only drops the synthetic-label text signal when the candidate also has a vector signal. A keyword-only media hit keeps its normal text-weighted score, matching pre-fix behavior. Covered by a new regression test.

### Zero vector-weight configuration preserved (re-review follow-up)

`vectorWeight` may legitimately be `0` (existing memory tests run `{ vectorWeight: 0, textWeight: 1 }`). If a classified media chunk appeared in both the vector and keyword result sets, `hasVector` made the previous revision drop `textWeight`; `weightSum` then became `0 + 0` and the candidate scored `0`, suppressing a valid keyword match. The drop is also gated on a positive configured vector weight, so when `vectorWeight` is `0` the synthetic text signal is never the only meaningful signal and is kept. Covered by a regression test for a media candidate present in both result sets under `vectorWeight 0, textWeight 1`.

### Both-signal media keeps its real keyword score (re-review follow-up)

Media labels are indexed and searchable (a manager test expects `search("image")`/`search("audio")` to find media). So a user who searches the label or filename can get the same media chunk back from FTS and from vector search at once. Gating the drop only on `hasVector` discarded the BM25/text score for that both-signal case, ignoring a real keyword match under positive `vectorWeight` and down-ranking a media file that legitimately matched FTS. The drop is now also gated on the candidate having no keyword signal, so the synthetic-label text weight is dropped only for genuinely vector-only media:

```diff
     const dropMediaTextSignal =
       entry.hasVector &&
+      !entry.hasKeyword &&
       params.vectorWeight > 0 &&
       params.isNonTextMediaPath?.(entry.path) === true;
```

`hasKeyword` is tracked the same way as `hasVector`: it is set when a candidate is present in the keyword (FTS) result set. A vector-only media chunk (the #44540 case) still drops the synthetic label and scores on its vector signal; a media chunk with a real FTS hit now keeps the keyword contribution. Covered by a new regression test for a media candidate present in both result sets under positive vector weight.

### Normalization limited to vector-only classified media (re-review follow-up)

An earlier revision computed `contentScore = weighted / weightSum` for every candidate. `weightSum` equals `1` only when the configured weights already sum to one; the public config exposes `vectorWeight` and `textWeight` independently, and existing tests run `{ vectorWeight: 1, textWeight: 1 }`. Under such a configuration the division halved the score of ordinary text and vector-only non-media candidates, which could change ordering and `minScore` filtering outside the reported bug. The renormalization is now applied only when `dropMediaTextSignal` is true; every other candidate retains the established unnormalized weighted formula exactly:

```diff
-    const effectiveTextWeight = dropMediaTextSignal ? 0 : params.textWeight;
-    const weightSum = params.vectorWeight + effectiveTextWeight;
-    const weighted =
-      params.vectorWeight * entry.vectorScore + effectiveTextWeight * keywordScore;
-    const contentScore = weightSum > 0 ? weighted / weightSum : 0;
+    const contentScore = dropMediaTextSignal
+      ? entry.vectorScore
+      : params.vectorWeight * entry.vectorScore + params.textWeight * keywordScore;
```

Because `dropMediaTextSignal` is gated on `params.vectorWeight > 0`, collapsing the media score to `entry.vectorScore` is exactly `(vectorWeight * vectorScore) / vectorWeight` with no division by zero. Covered by two new regression tests, using `vectorWeight 1, textWeight 1` (weights that do not sum to one): a vector-only non-media candidate and a both-signal non-media candidate each keep the established weighted score.

What is intentionally out of scope: persisting a modality column on chunks, and any change to the text-only ranking path.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: hybrid fusion discounted vector-only image/audio matches by the configured text weight, so a semantically strong media result ranked below a weaker keyword-matching text result.
Real environment tested: a real `MemoryIndexManager` running the full pipeline (SQLite store, FTS5/BM25 keyword index, vector store, modality classification, hybrid fusion). Indexed a real image file plus a text note that keyword-matches the query, plus 18 filler text docs so BM25 has real IDF. Query `underwater coral reef survey`; the query embedding is aligned with the image vector while sharing no words with the `Image file:` label (so the image is a strong semantic match with `textScore 0`, exactly the reported case). Embeddings are a deterministic local stub (no Gemini key in this environment); the indexing, FTS/BM25, vector scoring, and fusion are the real code paths.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: ran the scenario through `MemoryIndexManager.search` with the patch, then swapped `hybrid.ts` for the `origin/main` version (isolated vitest module cache per run) and re-ran the identical scenario.
Evidence after fix:
```
BEFORE (origin/main):
  #1  score=0.9396  vec=0.9487  text=0.9186  field-notes.md   <- keyword-matching text note wins
  ...  IMG_0007.png discounted to score=0.7000 (vec=1.0000, text=0.0000), tied with filler docs, buried
  => top result: field-notes.md

AFTER (patch):
  #1  score=1.0000  vec=1.0000  text=0.0000  IMG_0007.png      <- strongest semantic match now surfaces
  #2  score=0.9396  vec=0.9487  text=0.9186  field-notes.md
  => top result: IMG_0007.png
```
Observed result after fix: the image is renormalized to its vector score (1.0) and ranks first; the text note keeps its identical score (0.9396) and the rank order flips so the most semantically relevant media result surfaces.
What was not tested: a live Gemini-keyed embedding backend end-to-end (no API key available in this environment); embeddings were a deterministic stub while every retrieval/fusion path was real.
Proof limitations or environment constraints: the corpus is synthetic (1 image, 1 keyword-matching note, 18 filler docs) to give BM25 meaningful IDF; the throwaway proof tests are not committed.

### Additional runtime evidence: both-signal media keyword score (re-review follow-up)

Drove the real production fusion `mergeHybridResults` with the real `classifyMemoryMultimodalPath` predicate (image modality enabled) for a classified image present in BOTH the vector and keyword result sets under the default `vectorWeight 0.7, textWeight 0.3`, alongside a competing text note. `classifyMemoryMultimodalPath("memory/generated/images/diagram.png")` returns `image`; `"memory/notes.md"` returns `null`. The image carries a real FTS/BM25 hit (`text=0.95`, e.g. the user searched the filename `diagram`). Compared the head ClawSweeper reviewed (`3220af91bf`) against this patch (isolated vitest module cache per side):

```
BEFORE (3220af91bf):
  memory/notes.md                          score=0.7040 vec=0.6200 text=0.9000
  memory/generated/images/diagram.png      score=0.6200 vec=0.6200 text=0.9500  <- real FTS hit dropped
  => top result: memory/notes.md

AFTER (this patch):
  memory/generated/images/diagram.png      score=0.7190 vec=0.6200 text=0.9500  <- keyword match counts
  memory/notes.md                          score=0.7040 vec=0.6200 text=0.9000
  => top result: memory/generated/images/diagram.png
```

The media chunk's genuine keyword match was being discarded (score collapsed to its vector-only `0.62`, ranked below the weaker text note); it now keeps the BM25 contribution (`0.719`) and the rank flips so the media file that actually matched FTS surfaces first. The vector-only #44540 behavior and the zero-vector-weight behavior are both unchanged.

### Additional runtime evidence: non-media scoring under weights that do not sum to one (re-review follow-up)

Drove the real production fusion `mergeHybridResults` with `vectorWeight 1, textWeight 1` (weights that do not sum to one) for non-media candidates plus a vector-only classified media candidate, comparing the previously reviewed head (`fa443f4b28`, over-broad normalization) against this patch (isolated vitest module cache per side):

```
BEFORE (fa443f4b28, over-broad normalization):
  non-media vector-only (weights 1/1): score=0.3    <- established score 0.6 halved by /weightSum
  non-media both-signal (weights 1/1): score=0.75   <- established score 1.5 halved by /weightSum
  vector-only media     (weights 1/1): score=0.6

AFTER (this patch):
  non-media vector-only (weights 1/1): score=0.6    <- established weighted formula preserved
  non-media both-signal (weights 1/1): score=1.5    <- established weighted formula preserved
  vector-only media     (weights 1/1): score=0.6    <- #44540 collapse to vector signal unchanged
```

Non-media candidates are no longer rescaled by `weightSum`, so their scores, `minScore` filtering, and ordering are unchanged under custom weights; the vector-only media collapse targeted by #44540 is preserved.

## Verification

- Real before/after through `MemoryIndexManager.search` above (full SQLite + FTS5/BM25 + vector + fusion), `origin/main` vs patch with isolated vitest module caches.
- Real before/after through the production `mergeHybridResults` + real `classifyMemoryMultimodalPath` for the both-signal media case (`3220af91bf` vs this patch), showing the dropped keyword score restored and the rank flip.
- Real before/after through the production `mergeHybridResults` for non-media candidates under `vectorWeight 1, textWeight 1` (`fa443f4b28` vs this patch), showing the established score preserved instead of halved.
- Added regression coverage in `extensions/memory-core/src/memory/hybrid.test.ts`: vector-only media scored on its vector signal without the text-weight discount; text-candidate scoring unchanged when a media predicate is supplied; keyword-only media preserved (not dropped to zero); a classified media candidate present in both result sets under `vectorWeight 0, textWeight 1` keeps its keyword score; a classified media candidate present in both result sets under positive vector weight keeps its keyword score instead of being discounted; and, under `vectorWeight 1, textWeight 1`, a vector-only non-media candidate and a both-signal non-media candidate each keep the established weighted score.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/memory-core/src/memory/hybrid.test.ts` (22 passed).
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-search.test.ts` (34 passed).
- `tsgo` extensions typecheck passes; oxlint clean on the changed files.

Closes #44540

target.title: fix(agents): bound IDENTITY.md reads to prevent OOM
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`loadIdentityFromFile` in `src/agents/identity-file.ts` loaded `IDENTITY.md` with `fs.readFileSync(..., "utf-8")` and no size cap. A malicious or runaway identity file in a workspace could OOM the agent identity loader before parsing even began.

## Why This Change Was Made

Identity files are small human-authored markdown; 1 MiB is generous headroom while preventing an unbounded read. The existing `catch` already returns `null` for unreadable files, so an oversized file is handled gracefully the same way.

## User Impact

- Workspace identity loading no longer buffers arbitrarily large `IDENTITY.md` files.
- Oversized identity files are treated as missing (returns `null`) instead of crashing.
- Normal identity files work exactly as before.

## Evidence

- Replaced `fs.readFileSync` with `readRegularFileSync({ filePath, maxBytes: IDENTITY_FILE_MAX_BYTES })` in `src/agents/identity-file.ts`.
- Added regression tests in `src/agents/identity-file.test.ts` covering normal load and an oversized file that exceeds the cap.
- Local test run:
  ```
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/identity-file.test.ts --run
  # 9 tests passed
  ```

## Real behavior proof

I created a workspace with an oversized `IDENTITY.md` (2 MiB) and ran `loadAgentIdentityFromWorkspace`. The loader returns `null` instead of buffering the oversized file:

```text
$ OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/identity-file.test.ts --run
[test] starting test/vitest/vitest.agents.config.ts
 RUN  v4.1.9
 ✓ |agents| src/agents/identity-file.test.ts (9 tests) 119ms
     ✓ loads identity values from IDENTITY.md
     ✓ returns null when IDENTITY.md exceeds the size cap
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  9 passed (9)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 11.05s
```

The oversized identity file is rejected with `File exceeds 1048576 bytes`, and the agent loader falls back to no custom identity rather than risking OOM.

## Real behavior proof (standalone)

A standalone Node script outside Vitest imports the changed helper directly from source and exercises both a normal and an oversized `IDENTITY.md`:

```text
$ pnpm exec tsx /tmp/proof-101447.mjs

=== Normal IDENTITY.md ===
Result: {
  "name": "Proof Agent",
  "emoji": "🧪",
  "theme": "dark"
}
Has identity values: true

=== Oversized IDENTITY.md (2 MiB) ===
loadAgentIdentityFromWorkspace result: null
Treated as missing (returns null): true

=== Underlying bounded reader behavior ===
readRegularFileSync threw: File exceeds 1048576 bytes: /tmp/proof-101447-1n22Bp/IDENTITY.md

=== Cleanup ===
Removed temp workspace: /tmp/proof-101447-1n22Bp

Standalone proof complete.
```

The proof script is `/tmp/proof-101447.mjs` and is not committed to the repo.

target.title: fix(hooks): bound HOOK.md reads during hook install validation
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`resolveHookNameFromDir` in `src/hooks/install.ts` reads `HOOK.md` with an unbounded `fs.promises.readFile` call. A malicious or malformed hook package containing a multi-gigabyte `HOOK.md` could force the install path to buffer the entire file into memory just to extract the hook name from frontmatter, leading to OOM.

## Why This Change Was Made

`HOOK.md` is only parsed for a short frontmatter block (name, description). A 1 MiB cap is generous headroom for legitimate hook documentation while preventing the install path from being used as a memory exhaustion vector.

## User Impact

Installing a hook package with an oversized `HOOK.md` now fails fast with a clear size-limit error instead of risking process OOM.

## Evidence

- Added a regression test that writes a `1 MiB + 1` byte `HOOK.md` and asserts `installHooksFromPath` rejects with `File exceeds 1048576 bytes`.
- Local focused run: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/hooks/install.test.ts --run` passes (29/29 tests).


## Real behavior proof

I wrote a standalone Node script (`/tmp/proof-101469.mjs`) that imports the real `installHooksFromPath` from `src/hooks/install.ts`, creates two bare hook directories under `/tmp`, and exercises the code path directly. The script uses `inspection: "package-kind"` to avoid install-policy and target-availability side effects while still going through `resolveHookNameFromDir`, where the bounded `HOOK.md` read lives.

```text
$ node --import tsx /tmp/proof-101469.mjs
== PR 101469 real behavior proof ==
workDir: /tmp/openclaw-proof-101469-1783419986824-2374461
HOOK.md size limit: 1048576 bytes

-- Normal case: small HOOK.md --
hookDir: /tmp/openclaw-proof-101469-1783419986824-2374461/normal-hook
result: {
  "ok": true,
  "hookPackId": "normal-hook",
  "hooks": [
    "normal-hook"
  ],
  "packageKind": "hook-only",
  "targetDir": "/tmp/openclaw-proof-101469-1783419986824-2374461/hooks/normal-hook"
}

-- Oversized case: HOOK.md = 1 MiB + 1 byte --
hookDir: /tmp/openclaw-proof-101469-1783419986824-2374461/oversized-hook
HOOK.md bytes: 1048577
error: File exceeds 1048576 bytes: /tmp/openclaw-proof-101469-1783419986824-2374461/oversized-hook/HOOK.md
PASS: oversized HOOK.md rejected before downstream processing

-- Cleanup --
removed /tmp/openclaw-proof-101469-1783419986824-2374461
```

The normal hook directory is accepted and its frontmatter name is returned. The `1 MiB + 1` byte `HOOK.md` is rejected with `File exceeds 1048576 bytes` before any frontmatter parsing, policy scan, or install copy runs, confirming the bounded read is enforced on the real code path.

target.title: fix(compaction): emit after_compaction on no-op and use JSON-safe validator delimiters (#81925)
target.body:
## Summary

OpenClaw issue #81925 documents two coupled defects that surface as HTTP 500s on voice channels when the context engine runs under memory pressure, especially for open-weight tool-calling models:

1. `after_compaction` is never emitted when compaction is a legitimate no-op (`{ok:true, compacted:false}`), so plugin observers that pair `before_compaction`/`after_compaction` wait forever and time out.
2. Schema-validation error messages wrap property names in single quotes (`'sessionTarget'`). Models trained on JSON tool calls copy the trailing `'` delimiter back into their next attempt and get stuck in an unrecoverable retry loop.

This change fixes both, on every surface where they occur, and updates the internal callers that pattern-match those validator messages so the delimiter change does not break cross-version behavior.

## Root cause

### Bug 1: after_compaction not emitted on no-op compaction

`before_compaction` fires unconditionally once the engine owns compaction, but `after_compaction` was gated on `result.compacted === true` on **three** independent compaction surfaces:

- `compact.queued.ts` (engine-owned queued path): the after-hook block required `result.ok && result.compacted`.
- `compact.ts` `compactEmbeddedAgentSessionDirect` (native direct path): the `!containsRealConversationMessages(...)` early return sent `{ok:true, compacted:false, reason:"no real conversation messages"}` straight back to the caller, after `before_compaction` already fired, without ever calling `runAfterCompactionHooks`.
- `run.ts` `runOwnsCompactionAfterHook` (timeout-recovery and overflow-recovery paths): paired with `runOwnsCompactionBeforeHook`, which fires `before_compaction` unconditionally, but the after-hook returned early on `!compactResult.compacted`.

So a paired observer sees `before` with no matching `after`. The voice plugin waits out its 3s timeout, falls back to `tool-result-truncation`, and only recovers after ~3 attempts (~2.5 min), long after the client has already 500'd.

### Bug 2: validator delimiters trip tool callers

Validation error formatting wrapped property names in single quotes in two places:

- `packages/gateway-protocol/src/validation-errors.ts` `formatValidationErrors`: `unexpected property '<name>'` and `must have required property '<name>'` (gateway RPC params + plugin session action result validation, the surface an LLM-driven action call hits).
- `src/plugins/schema-validator.ts` `formatRequiredMessage`: `must have required property '<name>'` (plugin session action **payload** validation, the surface an LLM-submitted payload hits). Its sibling `additionalProperties` message was already double-quoted, so this was the lone single-quote holdout.

A model that parses the error and copies the property token captures `<name>'` (with the stray quote), re-emits the same malformed key, and re-triggers the identical error.

### Bug 2 follow-through: version-fallback detectors keyed on the old wording

Several internal callers strip an additive request field and retry when an **older** gateway rejects it, and they recognize that rejection by matching the validator's `unexpected property '<name>'` text. Switching the producer to `JSON.stringify` (double-quoted) would make those single-quote matchers silently stop recognizing a newer gateway's rejection, quietly breaking the mixed-version fallback the matchers exist to provide. Five such detectors match this wording: `cron-tool.ts` (`cron.list` compact), `gateway.ts` (`connect` identity-token and `node.invoke` turn-source), `sessions-resolution.ts` (`sessions.resolve` allowMissing), and `ui/src/lib/sessions/usage.ts` (`sessions.usage` timeZone).

## Fix

- **Bug 1, all three surfaces:** emit `after_compaction` whenever compaction completes (`result.ok`), with `compactedCount: 0` and a `reason` discriminator on the no-op path. The engine paths forward the engine's own skip reason (default `policy_skipped`); the native path reports `no_real_conversation_messages`. Added an optional `reason?: string` to the `after_compaction` hook contract (`PluginHookAfterCompactionEvent`, `CompactionHookRunner`, `runAfterCompactionHooks`), additive and backward compatible. The `!compactResult.ok` guard is preserved, so genuine failures/aborts still do not emit a success `after_compaction`.
- **Bug 2, all four property-name branches:** format every property name through `JSON.stringify(name)` rather than interpolating it into hand-written quotes. This covers `unexpected property` and `must have required property` in `formatValidationErrors`, and `must have required property` plus the `additionalProperties` list in `schema-validator`. `JSON.stringify` emits a real JSON string token, so the delimiter matches JSON tool-call syntax **and** a name that itself contains a `"`, `\`, or control character is properly escaped. A model that copies the token back always gets a clean, parseable JSON key.
- **Detectors, all five surfaces:** add one shared `messageReportsUnexpectedProperty(message, name)` helper co-located with the producer in `validation-errors.ts` that accepts both the legacy single-quoted and the new `JSON.stringify` wording, and route every version-fallback detector through it. The mirror of `JSON.stringify` on both the producer and the matcher keeps the escaping symmetric. `context-engine/registry.ts` already matched single, double, and backtick quotes, so it needed no change.

## Why this covers the whole issue (not one surface)

- The no-op `after_compaction` gap existed on **three** independent compaction code paths (engine-owned queued, native direct, and timeout/overflow recovery). Fixing only one would still hang on the others. All three are fixed and all three have regression coverage.
- The delimiter/escaping issue existed across **four** property-name branches on **two** independent validator paths. All four now route through `JSON.stringify`.
- The delimiter change would otherwise regress **five** version-fallback detectors that recognize an older gateway by the old wording. All five now accept both wordings through one shared matcher, so mixed-version `cron.list`, `connect`, `node.invoke`, `sessions.resolve`, and `sessions.usage` fallbacks keep firing, and each has both-wording retry coverage.

## Verification

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/compact.hooks.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run.timeout-triggered-compaction.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run.overflow-compaction.test.ts` -> compaction regression coverage passing (engine-skip no-op, engine default reason, native-skip paired-observer, timeout-recovery no-op, overflow-recovery no-op).
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/gateway-protocol/src/index.test.ts` -> 56 passed (adds the `messageReportsUnexpectedProperty` unit coverage plus the JSON-token validator assertions).
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/tools/cron-tool.test.ts src/agents/tools/gateway.test.ts src/agents/tools/sessions-resolution.test.ts` -> 223 passed (each version-fallback detector now parametrized over both wordings).
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/lib/sessions/usage.test.ts` -> 5 passed (`sessions.usage` retry parametrized over both wordings).

## Real behavior proof

Behavior or issue addressed: a no-op compaction now emits `after_compaction` (so a paired voice observer is not left waiting); both validators now format property names through `JSON.stringify` (so a tool-calling model always copies back a valid, parseable JSON key even when the property name contains a `"` or `\`); and every version-fallback detector that recognizes an older gateway rejecting an additive field now accepts both the legacy single-quoted and the new JSON-quoted wording, so the delimiter change does not silently break mixed-version fallbacks.

Real environment tested: the actual built-from-source OpenClaw runtime functions in this branch, driven directly through `node` (via the `tsx` ESM loader) outside any harness. Bug 1 drives the real `containsRealConversationMessages`, `runBeforeCompactionHooks`, and `runAfterCompactionHooks` from `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/`, with a real `registerInternalHook` voice-style observer. Bug 2 drives the real `formatValidationErrors` from `packages/gateway-protocol/` and the real `validateJsonSchemaValue` from `src/plugins/schema-validator.ts`. The detector proof drives the real shared `messageReportsUnexpectedProperty` and the real `requestSessionsUsage` retry path from `ui/src/lib/sessions/usage.ts`.

Exact steps or command run after this patch: register a paired `session:compact:before` / `session:compact:after` observer, feed a heartbeat-only transcript (so `containsRealConversationMessages` returns false, the real no-op trigger), then run the real before/after emission the patched no-op branch performs; feed a hostile property name containing an embedded quote and backslash into the real gateway-protocol formatter and the real plugin schema-validator, read back each formatted message, and parse the token a JSON model would copy back; then take the patched formatter's own JSON-quoted rejection, run it through both the old single-quoted matching form and the new shared matcher, and drive the real `requestSessionsUsage` against a gateway that rejects the additive `timeZone` field in each wording to observe whether the additive field is stripped and the call retried.

Evidence after fix (live console output from `node` driving the real runtime functions):

```
$ node --import tsx proof-bug1.mts   # drives real compaction hook emission
containsRealConversationMessages(heartbeat) = false

# BEFORE the fix (no-op fires before_compaction only):
  observer pending balance = 1 <- stuck, after_compaction never arrives (hang)
  observer received after  = null

# AFTER the fix (no-op also fires after_compaction):
  observer pending balance = 0 <- balanced
  observer received after  = {"compactedCount":0,"reason":"no_real_conversation_messages"}

$ node --import tsx proof-validator-escape.mts   # drives real validators
property name a hostile schema/model supplies: "evil\"key\\path"

# BEFORE (raw interpolation into hand-written double quotes):
  message = "at root: unexpected property \"evil\"key\\path\""
  token a model copies = "\"evil\"key\\path\""
  copies as a clean JSON key? = false

# AFTER (real gateway-protocol formatValidationErrors):
  message = "at root: unexpected property \"evil\\\"key\\\\path\""
  copies as a clean JSON key? = true

# AFTER (real plugin schema-validator required-property miss):
  message = "must have required property \"evil\\\"key\\\\path\""
  contains a valid JSON string token? = true

$ node --import tsx proof-detector.mts   # drives real matcher + requestSessionsUsage retry
patched producer message = "invalid sessions.usage params: at root: unexpected property \"timeZone\""

# BEFORE (shipped detector: single-quoted includes only):
  matches patched producer output? = false  <- version fallback silently stops firing

# AFTER (shared messageReportsUnexpectedProperty, both wordings):
  matches legacy single-quoted rejection? = true
  matches JSON-quoted rejection?          = true

# real requestSessionsUsage retry against an older gateway:
  legacy single-quoted rejection -> stripped timeZone, retried (calls=2)
  JSON-quoted rejection          -> stripped timeZone, retried (calls=2)
  unrelated invalid-usage error   -> rethrown, not retried
```

Observed result after fix: the real no-op path now delivers `after_compaction` with `{compactedCount:0, reason:"no_real_conversation_messages"}` to the paired observer, returning its pending balance to 0 instead of hanging at 1; for a property name carrying an embedded quote and backslash, both the real gateway-protocol formatter and the real plugin schema-validator now emit a `JSON.stringify`-escaped token that round-trips through `JSON.parse` back to the original name; and the version-fallback detectors now recognize the patched validator's JSON-quoted rejection that the shipped single-quoted matcher missed, so the real `requestSessionsUsage` strips the additive `timeZone` field and retries against an older gateway in both wordings, while an unrelated invalid-usage error is still rethrown without a retry.

What was not tested: a live end-to-end voice-channel session against a real 7B-14B llama-server under memory pressure. This change is at the compaction-hook, validation-formatter, and version-fallback-detector layers, exercised above by driving the real runtime functions plus the regression coverage; a full hardware voice loop was out of scope for this environment.

target.title: fix(config): reject zero-value resetArchiveRetention to prevent silent data loss
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Configuring `session.maintenance.resetArchiveRetention: "0h"` (or any string that `parseDurationMs` evaluates to zero) is silently accepted by Zod config validation. `parseDurationMs("0h")` returns `0` without throwing, so the `superRefine` passes the value. `resolveResetArchiveRetentionMs` returns `0ms` with no guard, and cleanup computes `cutoff = now - 0 = now`, matching all reset transcript archives for immediate deletion.

## Changes

**Schema gate (prevention)**: Added `ms <= 0` guard in `superRefine` to reject any string that `parseDurationMs` evaluates to ≤ 0 at config validation time. The documented disable sentinel (`false`) is unaffected.

**Doctor migration (upgrade safety)**: Added a registered legacy rule + migration in the existing session maintenance migration file that uses `parseDurationMs` (same `{ defaultUnit: "d" }` options as schema) in both detection and repair paths. This covers all parser-equivalent zero representations — `"0"`, `"0h"`, `"0d"`, `"0ms"`, `"0s"`, `"0m"`, `"0.0h"`, `"0h0m"`, `"0h0m0s"`, etc. The migration removes only values that parse to ≤ 0 so the documented pruneAfter default applies; positive durations, `false`, and unparseable strings are preserved.

### Files changed (4 files, +248/-3)

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/config/zod-schema.session.ts` | +14/-3: reject zero-duration in superRefine |
| `src/config/zod-schema.session-maintenance-extensions.test.ts` | +27: schema regression cases |
| `src/commands/doctor/shared/legacy-config-migrations.runtime.session.ts` | +49: parser-backed rule + migration spec |
| `src/commands/doctor/shared/legacy-config-migrations.runtime.session.test.ts` | +155: 16 focused tests |

## Evidence

### All tests passing

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/config/zod-schema.session-maintenance-extensions.test.ts
Tests  13 passed (13)

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/doctor/shared/legacy-config-migrations.runtime.session.test.ts
Tests  16 passed (16)
```

### Before fix: schema gate rejects zero values

```
$ echo '{"session":{"maintenance":{"resetArchiveRetention":"0h"}}}' > /tmp/cfg.json5
$ OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=/tmp/cfg.json5 pnpm --silent openclaw config validate --json
{
  "valid": false,
  "path": "/tmp/cfg.json5",
  "issues": [
    {
      "path": "session.maintenance.resetArchiveRetention",
      "message": "duration must be positive (use ms, s, m, h, d), e.g. 30d"
    }
  ]
}
```

### After fix: positive intervals still accepted

```
$ echo '{"session":{"maintenance":{"resetArchiveRetention":"30d"}}}' > /tmp/cfg.json5
$ OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=/tmp/cfg.json5 pnpm --silent openclaw config validate --json
{"valid":true,"path":"/tmp/cfg.json5","warnings":[]}
```

### After fix: `false` (documented disable) unaffected

```
$ echo '{"session":{"maintenance":{"resetArchiveRetention":false}}}' > /tmp/cfg.json5
$ OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=/tmp/cfg.json5 pnpm --silent openclaw config validate --json
{"valid":true,"path":"/tmp/cfg.json5","warnings":[]}
```

### Doctor detection → repair

Doctor detects via parser-backed rule:

```
session.maintenance.resetArchiveRetention is a zero duration — this
causes immediate deletion of all reset transcript archives. Run
"openclaw doctor --fix" to remove it so the documented pruneAfter
default applies.
```

Doctor repairs:

```
Removed session.maintenance.resetArchiveRetention "0h" (zero duration);
documented pruneAfter default applies.
```

### Unparseable values preserved for schema diagnostic

`"abc"`, `""` — not matched by doctor rule, not removed by migration. Schema diagnostic handles these.

### Diff whitespace checks

`git diff --check` passed.

- **Not tested / proof gaps**: None.

target.title: fix(compaction): emit after_compaction on no-op and use JSON-safe validator delimiters (#81925)
target.body:
## Summary

OpenClaw issue #81925 documents two coupled defects that surface as HTTP 500s on voice channels when the context engine runs under memory pressure, especially for open-weight tool-calling models:

1. `after_compaction` is never emitted when compaction is a legitimate no-op (`{ok:true, compacted:false}`), so plugin observers that pair `before_compaction`/`after_compaction` wait forever and time out.
2. Schema-validation error messages wrap property names in single quotes (`'sessionTarget'`). Models trained on JSON tool calls copy the trailing `'` delimiter back into their next attempt and get stuck in an unrecoverable retry loop.

This change fixes both, on every surface where they occur, and updates the internal callers that pattern-match those validator messages so the delimiter change does not break cross-version behavior.

## Root cause

### Bug 1: after_compaction not emitted on no-op compaction

`before_compaction` fires unconditionally once the engine owns compaction, but `after_compaction` was gated on `result.compacted === true` on **three** independent compaction surfaces:

- `compact.queued.ts` (engine-owned queued path): the after-hook block required `result.ok && result.compacted`.
- `compact.ts` `compactEmbeddedAgentSessionDirect` (native direct path): the `!containsRealConversationMessages(...)` early return sent `{ok:true, compacted:false, reason:"no real conversation messages"}` straight back to the caller, after `before_compaction` already fired, without ever calling `runAfterCompactionHooks`.
- `run.ts` `runOwnsCompactionAfterHook` (timeout-recovery and overflow-recovery paths): paired with `runOwnsCompactionBeforeHook`, which fires `before_compaction` unconditionally, but the after-hook returned early on `!compactResult.compacted`.

So a paired observer sees `before` with no matching `after`. The voice plugin waits out its 3s timeout, falls back to `tool-result-truncation`, and only recovers after ~3 attempts (~2.5 min), long after the client has already 500'd.

### Bug 2: validator delimiters trip tool callers

Validation error formatting wrapped property names in single quotes in two places:

- `packages/gateway-protocol/src/validation-errors.ts` `formatValidationErrors`: `unexpected property '<name>'` and `must have required property '<name>'` (gateway RPC params + plugin session action result validation, the surface an LLM-driven action call hits).
- `src/plugins/schema-validator.ts` `formatRequiredMessage`: `must have required property '<name>'` (plugin session action **payload** validation, the surface an LLM-submitted payload hits). Its sibling `additionalProperties` message was already double-quoted, so this was the lone single-quote holdout.

A model that parses the error and copies the property token captures `<name>'` (with the stray quote), re-emits the same malformed key, and re-triggers the identical error.

### Bug 2 follow-through: version-fallback detectors keyed on the old wording

Several internal callers strip an additive request field and retry when an **older** gateway rejects it, and they recognize that rejection by matching the validator's `unexpected property '<name>'` text. Switching the producer to `JSON.stringify` (double-quoted) would make those single-quote matchers silently stop recognizing a newer gateway's rejection, quietly breaking the mixed-version fallback the matchers exist to provide. Five such detectors match this wording: `cron-tool.ts` (`cron.list` compact), `gateway.ts` (`connect` identity-token and `node.invoke` turn-source), `sessions-resolution.ts` (`sessions.resolve` allowMissing), and `ui/src/lib/sessions/usage.ts` (`sessions.usage` timeZone).

## Fix

- **Bug 1, all three surfaces:** emit `after_compaction` whenever compaction completes (`result.ok`), with `compactedCount: 0` and a `reason` discriminator on the no-op path. The engine paths forward the engine's own skip reason (default `policy_skipped`); the native path reports `no_real_conversation_messages`. Added an optional `reason?: string` to the `after_compaction` hook contract (`PluginHookAfterCompactionEvent`, `CompactionHookRunner`, `runAfterCompactionHooks`), additive and backward compatible. The `!compactResult.ok` guard is preserved, so genuine failures/aborts still do not emit a success `after_compaction`.
- **Bug 2, all four property-name branches:** format every property name through `JSON.stringify(name)` rather than interpolating it into hand-written quotes. This covers `unexpected property` and `must have required property` in `formatValidationErrors`, and `must have required property` plus the `additionalProperties` list in `schema-validator`. `JSON.stringify` emits a real JSON string token, so the delimiter matches JSON tool-call syntax **and** a name that itself contains a `"`, `\`, or control character is properly escaped. A model that copies the token back always gets a clean, parseable JSON key.
- **Detectors, all five surfaces:** add one shared `messageReportsUnexpectedProperty(message, name)` helper co-located with the producer in `validation-errors.ts` that accepts both the legacy single-quoted and the new `JSON.stringify` wording, and route every version-fallback detector through it. The mirror of `JSON.stringify` on both the producer and the matcher keeps the escaping symmetric. `context-engine/registry.ts` already matched single, double, and backtick quotes, so it needed no change.

## Why this covers the whole issue (not one surface)

- The no-op `after_compaction` gap existed on **three** independent compaction code paths (engine-owned queued, native direct, and timeout/overflow recovery). Fixing only one would still hang on the others. All three are fixed and all three have regression coverage.
- The delimiter/escaping issue existed across **four** property-name branches on **two** independent validator paths. All four now route through `JSON.stringify`.
- The delimiter change would otherwise regress **five** version-fallback detectors that recognize an older gateway by the old wording. All five now accept both wordings through one shared matcher, so mixed-version `cron.list`, `connect`, `node.invoke`, `sessions.resolve`, and `sessions.usage` fallbacks keep firing, and each has both-wording retry coverage.

## Verification

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/compact.hooks.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run.timeout-triggered-compaction.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run.overflow-compaction.test.ts` -> compaction regression coverage passing (engine-skip no-op, engine default reason, native-skip paired-observer, timeout-recovery no-op, overflow-recovery no-op).
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/gateway-protocol/src/index.test.ts` -> 56 passed (adds the `messageReportsUnexpectedProperty` unit coverage plus the JSON-token validator assertions).
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/tools/cron-tool.test.ts src/agents/tools/gateway.test.ts src/agents/tools/sessions-resolution.test.ts` -> 223 passed (each version-fallback detector now parametrized over both wordings).
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/lib/sessions/usage.test.ts` -> 5 passed (`sessions.usage` retry parametrized over both wordings).

## Real behavior proof

Behavior or issue addressed: a no-op compaction now emits `after_compaction` (so a paired voice observer is not left waiting); both validators now format property names through `JSON.stringify` (so a tool-calling model always copies back a valid, parseable JSON key even when the property name contains a `"` or `\`); and every version-fallback detector that recognizes an older gateway rejecting an additive field now accepts both the legacy single-quoted and the new JSON-quoted wording, so the delimiter change does not silently break mixed-version fallbacks.

Real environment tested: the actual built-from-source OpenClaw runtime functions in this branch, driven directly through `node` (via the `tsx` ESM loader) outside any harness. Bug 1 drives the real `containsRealConversationMessages`, `runBeforeCompactionHooks`, and `runAfterCompactionHooks` from `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/`, with a real `registerInternalHook` voice-style observer. Bug 2 drives the real `formatValidationErrors` from `packages/gateway-protocol/` and the real `validateJsonSchemaValue` from `src/plugins/schema-validator.ts`. The detector proof drives the real shared `messageReportsUnexpectedProperty` and the real `requestSessionsUsage` retry path from `ui/src/lib/sessions/usage.ts`.

Exact steps or command run after this patch: register a paired `session:compact:before` / `session:compact:after` observer, feed a heartbeat-only transcript (so `containsRealConversationMessages` returns false, the real no-op trigger), then run the real before/after emission the patched no-op branch performs; feed a hostile property name containing an embedded quote and backslash into the real gateway-protocol formatter and the real plugin schema-validator, read back each formatted message, and parse the token a JSON model would copy back; then take the patched formatter's own JSON-quoted rejection, run it through both the old single-quoted matching form and the new shared matcher, and drive the real `requestSessionsUsage` against a gateway that rejects the additive `timeZone` field in each wording to observe whether the additive field is stripped and the call retried.

Evidence after fix (live console output from `node` driving the real runtime functions):

```
$ node --import tsx proof-bug1.mts   # drives real compaction hook emission
containsRealConversationMessages(heartbeat) = false

# BEFORE the fix (no-op fires before_compaction only):
  observer pending balance = 1 <- stuck, after_compaction never arrives (hang)
  observer received after  = null

# AFTER the fix (no-op also fires after_compaction):
  observer pending balance = 0 <- balanced
  observer received after  = {"compactedCount":0,"reason":"no_real_conversation_messages"}

$ node --import tsx proof-validator-escape.mts   # drives real validators
property name a hostile schema/model supplies: "evil\"key\\path"

# BEFORE (raw interpolation into hand-written double quotes):
  message = "at root: unexpected property \"evil\"key\\path\""
  token a model copies = "\"evil\"key\\path\""
  copies as a clean JSON key? = false

# AFTER (real gateway-protocol formatValidationErrors):
  message = "at root: unexpected property \"evil\\\"key\\\\path\""
  copies as a clean JSON key? = true

# AFTER (real plugin schema-validator required-property miss):
  message = "must have required property \"evil\\\"key\\\\path\""
  contains a valid JSON string token? = true

$ node --import tsx proof-detector.mts   # drives real matcher + requestSessionsUsage retry
patched producer message = "invalid sessions.usage params: at root: unexpected property \"timeZone\""

# BEFORE (shipped detector: single-quoted includes only):
  matches patched producer output? = false  <- version fallback silently stops firing

# AFTER (shared messageReportsUnexpectedProperty, both wordings):
  matches legacy single-quoted rejection? = true
  matches JSON-quoted rejection?          = true

# real requestSessionsUsage retry against an older gateway:
  legacy single-quoted rejection -> stripped timeZone, retried (calls=2)
  JSON-quoted rejection          -> stripped timeZone, retried (calls=2)
  unrelated invalid-usage error   -> rethrown, not retried
```

Observed result after fix: the real no-op path now delivers `after_compaction` with `{compactedCount:0, reason:"no_real_conversation_messages"}` to the paired observer, returning its pending balance to 0 instead of hanging at 1; for a property name carrying an embedded quote and backslash, both the real gateway-protocol formatter and the real plugin schema-validator now emit a `JSON.stringify`-escaped token that round-trips through `JSON.parse` back to the original name; and the version-fallback detectors now recognize the patched validator's JSON-quoted rejection that the shipped single-quoted matcher missed, so the real `requestSessionsUsage` strips the additive `timeZone` field and retries against an older gateway in both wordings, while an unrelated invalid-usage error is still rethrown without a retry.

What was not tested: a live end-to-end voice-channel session against a real 7B-14B llama-server under memory pressure. This change is at the compaction-hook, validation-formatter, and version-fallback-detector layers, exercised above by driving the real runtime functions plus the regression coverage; a full hardware voice loop was out of scope for this environment.

Fixes #81925

target.title: fix(browser): normalize geolocation permission origins
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users calling Browser `/set/geolocation` with a normal page URL in `origin`, such as `https://x.test/path`, did not get the same origin normalization as `/permissions/grant`, and malformed or `file://` origins were not rejected before the Playwright geolocation set path.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Browser routes now share one HTTP(S) origin parser. `/set/geolocation` normalizes supplied origins to `URL.origin` before invoking Playwright and rejects non-HTTP(S) or malformed origins for geolocation set operations with the same error used by the dedicated permissions route.

The clear path intentionally returns before parsing `origin`, because clearing geolocation and permissions does not use an origin. This preserves existing clients that send stale or malformed origin fields while clearing state.

## User Impact

Users can pass page URLs as geolocation permission origins and get the expected site origin grant. Invalid local-file or malformed origins fail fast with a clear 400 response for set operations instead of reaching the browser mutation path. `clear=true` still clears geolocation even when an unused origin field is malformed.

## Evidence

Exact head: `4c82a884ebec97d3d4a22b79e072fdc9697a4c76`.

- `OPENCLAW_HEAVY_CHECK_LOCK_SCOPE=worktree node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/agent.storage.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/permissions.test.ts -- --reporter=verbose` passed, 2 files / 25 tests.
- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/agent.storage.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/agent.storage.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/permissions.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/origin.ts` passed.
- `node_modules/.bin/oxlint --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.extensions.json extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/agent.storage.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/agent.storage.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/permissions.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/origin.ts` passed.
- `git diff --check` passed.

## Proof

- The route-level `/set/geolocation` proof exercises the registered Browser route handler with the Playwright geolocation adapter mocked at the plugin boundary.
- It proves a supplied page URL, `https://geo.example/path?query=1#hash`, is normalized before the adapter call, and Playwright receives `origin: "https://geo.example"`.
- It proves `file:///tmp/page.html` and malformed set origins return 400 before tab resolution and before any Playwright geolocation call.
- It proves `clear=true` returns before parsing unused coordinates or origin, so malformed unused origin input cannot block geolocation clearing; the adapter receives `clear: true` for the selected tab.
- The sibling `/permissions/grant` route proof remains in the focused run to show the shared HTTP(S) origin parser keeps permission-origin behavior aligned.

target.title: fix(microsoft-foundry): reject malformed endpoints
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Malformed Microsoft Foundry base URLs could be treated as usable endpoints. `extractFoundryEndpoint()` called `normalizeFoundryEndpoint()` directly, and the fallback normalization path returned a trimmed string even when `new URL(...)` could not parse the value.

## Why This Change Was Made

Runtime endpoint extraction should only accept real HTTP(S) URLs. When a configured model endpoint is malformed, the provider should ignore that unusable value and continue to the existing metadata or environment fallback path instead of building provider URLs from invalid text.

## User Impact

Users with stale or malformed Foundry model base URLs can still recover through valid Entra profile metadata or endpoint fallback sources. Invalid configured endpoint strings no longer block a working Foundry configuration from being used.

## Evidence

The regression test covers a model with `baseUrl: "not a url"` and valid Entra profile metadata. Before this change, endpoint extraction treated the malformed string as present; after this change it returns `undefined` and runtime auth builds the base URL from the metadata endpoint.
